newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra lifts Swedish shares to all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Astra lifts Swedish shares to all-time high.

text.p: A 2.3 percent jump by drug company Astra helped lift the Swedish sharemarket to a record high close.
The bourse's general index rose 0.98 percent to 2,086.08, breaking a record set on September 27. Turnover was heavy at 5.2 billion crowns.
Astra rose 6.50 crowns to 286.50 on market rumours that Chief Executive Hakan Mogren was set to resign.
Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby dismissed the rumour as baseless. "It seems to be a widespread rumour but that's what's driving the share. I believe it's baseless," he said.
Some 4.5 million Astra shares changed hands, the highest volume in one day since June 13.
Appliance maker Electrolux leapt 13.50 crowns to 386.
"The share is just recovering losses after Whirlpool's profit warning last week," one broker said.
Vehicle maker Volvo rose 2.50 crowns to 145 after news from the Paris car show that it planned to raise the production of S40/V40 cars to 115,000 in 1997.
The banking sector was the only one to fall.
Handelsbanken, which closed up three crowns to 166, said a merger between it and S-E-Banken was not on the agenda. S-E-Banken fell one crown to 57.
